The rolling hills of the Ardennes provide a stunning backdrop to this cathedral of speed. It's a truly unique and special place.

The air is thick with anticipation. The rumble of the engines echoes through the forests as the drivers line up on the grid.
Spa is a circuit that tests both car and driver to the absolute limit. The fans know it, and they're here to witness history unfold.
The smell of fuel and burning rubber fills the air, a familiar scent that tells you you're at Spa-Francorchamps.

You can feel the energy radiating from the crowd. They know they're witnessing something special at this iconic circuit.

Michael Schumacher made his debut here in 1991, marking the start of a legendary career. Spa holds a special place in the hearts of many.
Remember Damon Hill's incredible victory in 1998? The Jordan team secured a memorable 1-2 finish after a chaotic race.
Spa has been the scene of many championship-defining moments over the years. Today could be another chapter in that story.

The Eau Rouge/Raidillon complex has seen countless incidents and near misses over the years. A test of bravery and precision.
Ayrton Senna's masterful performances at Spa are legendary. He conquered this challenging circuit with incredible skill and determination.

cornerCallouts: The drivers are now approaching La Source, that tight hairpin which is crucial for a good run down the hill.
Next up, it's the legendary Eau Rouge and Raidillon complex. A true test of nerve and car performance.
They're powering down the Kemmel Straight now, reaching incredible speeds before braking hard for Les Combes.
The drivers navigate Malmedy, setting themselves up for the run through Rivage.
Here they come into Pouhon, one of the fastest and most challenging corners on the entire Formula 1 calendar.
A good exit from Stavelot is crucial for a strong run towards the final chicane.
They are approaching Blanchimont now, another high-speed corner that demands respect.
The Bus Stop chicane is the final challenge before the start/finish straight, offering a last-gasp overtaking opportunity.
strategyPoints: Tire degradation is always a major factor here at Spa. Expect to see drivers managing their rubber throughout the race on this abrasive 7.004km circuit.
The long lap length and high speeds mean that fuel consumption will be a concern. Teams will be carefully monitoring their fuel levels.
With such a long lap, the pit lane time loss is significant. Teams will need to carefully consider when to bring their drivers in.
The weather here is notoriously unpredictable. A well-timed pit stop for intermediate tires can make all the difference.
Overtaking can be difficult at Spa, but the DRS zones on the Kemmel Straight and the run to Les Combes provide opportunities.
The optimal pit window is likely to be quite wide, giving teams some flexibility in their strategy.
A one-stop strategy is theoretically possible, but it will require careful tire management. A two-stop strategy may offer more flexibility and pace.
With the long straights, straight-line speed is crucial. Teams will be looking to optimize their downforce levels for both speed and cornering performance.
weatherCommentary: The radar is showing a chance of showers later in the race. The Ardennes mountains are known for their microclimates, so anything is possible.
The wind is picking up here at Spa, which could affect the car balance and make things tricky for the drivers.
The temperature is dropping, which could lead to reduced grip levels. Teams will need to adjust their tire pressures accordingly.
The sun is shining now, but the clouds are gathering. Don't be surprised if we see some rain before the end of the race.
It's a beautiful day here in the Ardennes, but the weather can change in an instant. Keep an eye on those skies!
gridWalkQuotes: "Spa is all about commitment," says Lando Norris. "You have to be brave through Eau Rouge and Raidillon to get a good lap time."
"This track is a real challenge," says Carlos Sainz. "You need a car that's good in both the high-speed corners and the slower sections."
"I love racing at Spa," says Lewis Hamilton. "It's one of the most iconic circuits in the world, and it always provides a great race."
"The weather here is always a factor," says Max Verstappen. "You have to be ready for anything."
"We've been working hard on our setup for this track," says Charles Leclerc. "Hopefully, we can have a strong result."
"Spa is a track that rewards precision," says George Russell. "You have to be inch-perfect to get the most out of it."
"Overtaking is difficult here, but not impossible," says Fernando Alonso. "We'll be looking for every opportunity."
"The key to a good lap at Spa is finding the right rhythm," says Sergio Perez. "You have to flow through the corners and carry as much speed as possible."
